Baking: 80 minutes|Difficulty=3 | Image = [[Image:Sachertorte_DSC03027.JPG|300px]] }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Austria|Austrian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] '''Sachertorte''' (Ger. ˈzɑxər ˈtɔrtə; Eng.ˈsɑkər ˈtɔrt; Ger. zah-khuhr tawr-tuh; sah-ker tawrt); is a [[Cookbook:chocolate|chocolate]] [[Cookbook:cake|cake]], invented by Franz Sacher in 1832 in Vienna, Austria. It is one of the most famous Viennese culinary specialties. The word is sometimes split into Sacher torte. The cake consists of two layers of dense, not overly sweet chocolate cake with a thin layer of [[Cookbook:apricot|apricot]] jam in the middle and dark chocolate icing with shreds of chocolate on the top and sides. This is traditionally eaten with whipped cream, as most Viennese consider the Sachertorte too "dry" to be eaten without. The trademark for the "Original Sachertorte" was registered by the Hotel Sacher, which was built in 1876 by the son of Franz Sacher. That original recipe is a well-kept secret. ==Ingredients== === '''Cake''' === *6 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]] *200 [[Cookbook:gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Caster sugar|caster sugar]] *100 [[Cookbook:gram|g]] unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], soft but not melted *125 [[Cookbook:gram|g]] dark (semi-sweet or [[Cookbook:Bittersweet chocolate|bittersweet]]) eating [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate]], melted *125 [[Cookbook:gram|g]] plain [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] *5 [[Cookbook:mL|ml]] [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] extract === '''Assembly''' === *150 [[Cookbook:g|g]] [[Cookbook:Apricot|apricot]] [[Cookbook:Jam|jam]] *150 [[Cookbook:g|g]] (100 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Golden Syrup|golden syrup]] *150 [[Cookbook:gram|g]] dark eating [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate]] (semi-sweet or [[Cookbook:Bittersweet chocolate|bittersweet]]) ==Equipment== * [[Cookbook:Oven|Oven]] * 2 mixing bowls * [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] * [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]] * [[Cookbook:Scale|Scales]] * [[Cookbook:Microwave Oven|Microwave oven]] with microwaveable bowl or a saucepan * Round [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake tin]] (preferably springform with removable bottom) about 20 cm diameter and 10 cm high * A cup or similar as temporary egg yolk container * [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|Greaseproof paper]] ==Procedure== === '''Cake''' === #Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 170°C. #[[Cookbook:Separating Eggs|Separate]] the eggs, putting the whites in a mixing bowl. #[[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] the whites until fairly stiff and foamy. Add three quarters of the sugar. [[Cookbook:Whipping|Whip]] until fully stiff and foamy, incorporating as much air as possible. #[[Cookbook:Creaming|Cream]] the remaining sugar with the butter and vanilla until pale and creamy. #Gently mix in the egg yolks, then the molten chocolate. #[[Cookbook:Folding|Fold]] the egg white foam into the batter. #[[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] the flour over the batter, carefully avoiding lumps of flour. Mix very gently, folding the ingredients together. Ensure the heavy chocolate does not all end up at the bottom of the bowl. #Line the cake tin with greaseproof paper, and fill it with the batter. #[[Cookbook:Bake|Bake]] at 170°C for about 70 minutes. #Allow to cool in the tin upside down until the cake reaches room temperature (about 30 minutes). === '''Assembly''' === # Microwave the jam until it melts. # Cut the cake body in half horizontally and place the halves with inner (cut) faces uppermost. # Pour the molten jam onto both halves of the cake, and allow it to soak in. # Reassemble the cake, with cut surfaces together. Allow the surface to cool again. # Microwave the golden syrup and chocolate together until the syrup just starts to bubble. Stir until they are smoothly mixed, then cool to about 25°C. This mixture should be spreadable and able to support a thickness of about 2 mm on a vertical surface (test on the wall of the bowl) yet return to shiny soon after being spread. If it is too hard or soft, add more golden syrup or chocolate and go back to the microwaving stage. # Spread cake body with the glaze. Leave it to set. ==Notes, tips, and variations== *The little bubbles in the egg white foam are what inflate the cake. Do not accidentally get any fat (from the egg yolks, butter, or chocolate) in the egg white mix or it will not foam properly. *Do not allow flour lumps in the mix, because lumps of white flour show up badly in this brown cake. *To get the traditional perfectly cylindrical shape, trim the cake body into a circle with vertical edges, and cut the top off flat before glazing. *Adding alcohol to the cake is not a good idea. It is already very moist, and more liquid will make it soggy. *Don't use white chocolate in the cake body because it is fairly unnoticeable in flavour and colour, leaving only the moistening effect. *Don't use self-raising flour, which creates large bubbles in the cake. *If carried out in the order above, no tool should need to be washed up more than once. *There are several other recipes for [[Cookbook:Sachertorte|Sachertorte]]—some use even more eggs in the cake and egg and cream in the glaze. ==References== *Original Source: [http://duramecho.com/Food/Sachertorte/index.html Duramecho Sachertorte] included here in slightly edited format under [http://www.gnu.org/copyleft/gpl.html GNU General Public License] *The exact amount of syrup needed in the glaze depends on the sugar content of the chocolate. You want about equal weights of syrup and chocolate for normal UK plain eating chocolate (which is 50% cocoa solids) but more syrup if using darker (e.g. 70%) chocolate. steps.text: Preheat the oven to 170°C.
Separate the eggs, putting the whites in a mixing bowl.

steps.text: Whisk the whites until fairly stiff and foamy. Add three quarters of the sugar. Whip until fully stiff and foamy, incorporating as much air as possible.
steps.sourceText: Whisk the whites until fairly stiff and foamy. Add three quarters of the sugar. Whip until fully stiff and foamy, incorporating as much air as possible.

steps.text: Cream the remaining sugar with the butter and vanilla until pale and creamy.
steps.sourceText: Cream the remaining sugar with the butter and vanilla until pale and creamy.

steps.text: Gently mix in the egg yolks, then the molten chocolate.

steps.text: Fold the egg white foam into the batter.
steps.sourceText: Fold the egg white foam into the batter.

steps.text: Sift the flour over the batter, carefully avoiding lumps of flour. Mix very gently, folding the ingredients together. Ensure the heavy chocolate does not all end up at the bottom of the bowl.

steps.text: Line the cake tin with greaseproof paper, and fill it with the batter.

steps.text: Bake at 170°C for about 70 minutes.
Allow to cool in the tin upside down until the cake reaches room temperature (about 30 minutes).
steps.sourceText: Allow to cool in the tin upside down until the cake reaches room temperature (about 30 minutes).

steps.text: Microwave the jam until it melts.
steps.sourceText: Microwave the jam until it melts.

steps.text: Cut the cake body in half horizontally and place the halves with inner (cut) faces uppermost.
steps.sourceText: Cut the cake body in half horizontally and place the halves with inner (cut) faces uppermost.

steps.text: Pour the molten jam onto both halves of the cake, and allow it to soak in.
steps.sourceText: Pour the molten jam onto both halves of the cake, and allow it to soak in.

steps.text: Reassemble the cake, with cut surfaces together. Allow the surface to cool again.

steps.text: Microwave the golden syrup and chocolate together until the syrup just starts to bubble. Stir until they are smoothly mixed, then cool to about 25°C. This mixture should be spreadable and able to support a thickness of about 2 mm on a vertical surface (test on the wall of the bowl) yet return to shiny soon after being spread. If it is too hard or soft, add more golden syrup or chocolate and go back to the microwaving stage.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 170°C.
Separate the eggs, putting the whites in a mixing bowl.
Whisk the whites until fairly stiff and foamy. Add three quarters of the sugar. Whip until fully stiff and foamy, incorporating as much air as possible.
Cream the remaining sugar with the butter and vanilla until pale and creamy.
Gently mix in the egg yolks, then the molten chocolate.
Fold the egg white foam into the batter.
Sift the flour over the batter, carefully avoiding lumps of flour. Mix very gently, folding the ingredients together. Ensure the heavy chocolate does not all end up at the bottom of the bowl.
Line the cake tin with greaseproof paper, and fill it with the batter.
Bake at 170°C for about 70 minutes.
Allow to cool in the tin upside down until the cake reaches room temperature (about 30 minutes).
Microwave the jam until it melts.
Cut the cake body in half horizontally and place the halves with inner (cut) faces uppermost.
Pour the molten jam onto both halves of the cake, and allow it to soak in.
Reassemble the cake, with cut surfaces together. Allow the surface to cool again.

Microwave the golden syrup and chocolate together until the syrup just starts to bubble. Stir until they are smoothly mixed, then cool to about 25°C. This mixture should be spreadable and able to support a thickness of about 2 mm on a vertical surface (test on the wall of the bowl) yet return to shiny soon after being spread. If it is too hard or soft, add more golden syrup or chocolate and go back to the microwaving stage.
Spread cake body with the glaze. Leave it to set.
